[MARCHAND]  Smith should review the “First Take” tape and consider his words one more time.

On Wednesday morning on his show, “First Take,” Smith belittled Philadelphia Eagles All-Pro tackle Lane Johnson for retiring four games into the season, ending an illustrious career. Johnson, whose battles with his mental health have been well-chronicled, alluded to these issues in his announcement.

f Smith, who has professional roots in Philadelphia, made a call or two, he could find out how profound Johnson’s situation is. Even without picking up the phone, it is easy to discover that part of Johnson’s legacy is how open, honest and courageous he has been in talking about his struggles, including missing three games in 2021 from withdrawal symptoms after cycling off SSRI antidepressants.

Instead, Smith did television.

Eagles-Panthers Film Review: Sean Mannion should probably be replaced

I don't think I've ever seen an offense film review this despondent in over 6 years

Summary from the article:

Those of you who have read my work for a while will know that I rarely call for a player to be benched or a coach to be fired. I would much rather explain what is going wrong and look for ways to fix it. But after watching the Eagles’ offense against the Panthers, I think Sean Mannion (you can add more if you want) should probably go. This under-center, outside zone offense he brought in has been dreadful, and I don’t see a coach who looks ready to solve the problems his own system is creating. With so little coaching experience, he looks completely out of his depth.

[AshlynSullivan] Eagles' offense is done making excuses as Mannion makes some major changes

“Mannion instructed the entire offense to arrive at the practice facility earlier than usual Monday morning.

Instead of breaking into position groups, more than 40 offensive players gathered in the team’s large film room. Mannion then walked through all 64 offensive snaps from the Panthers game, breaking down what went wrong and holding players accountable to their mistakes. The game review as an entire offense took an hour and a half.

The offensive players were then instructed to go to their position group rooms where they watched the entire game ... again.

Mannion was accountable about the mistakes he made in play-calling against Carolina, but his primary focus was on the opportunities players left on the field.”
